html:
The Kaw, or Kansa, are a Dhegiha Siouan people of the lower Missouri and Kansas river valleys, who gave their name to the Kansas River and the state of Kansas. Their language is close to those of the Osage, Omaha and Ponca.

They lived in earth lodge villages along the rivers, growing maize, beans and squash, and rode out to hunt bison on the plains. French traders reached them in the 1700s, and the Lewis and Clark expedition passed through their land in 1804. Treaties in 1825 and 1846 cut their land down to a small reservation at Council Grove on the Santa Fe Trail, and in 1873 they were moved to Indian Territory.

Charles Curtis, a Kaw citizen, became Vice President of the United States in 1929. See Kaw (Oklahoma) for their later lands.
